title: When Reasoning Leaves the Transcript
subtitle: A Research Program for Hybrid Computation, Semantic Boundaries, and Consequential Agency
abstract: In Hybrid Reasoning Agents, Jiaru Zou, Yunzhe Qi, Sirui Chen, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Pan Lu, Jingrui He, and James Zou describe agents that combine text-based interaction with internal computation in continuous representations. This separation raises an engineering question: what must cross from private computation into the world for another participant to interpret a proposal, assess its evidence, determine its authority, and inherit its remaining obligations? This research-program essay develops a recipient- and task-relative account of boundary sufficiency. Its central test constructs source situations that yield the same outward record but legitimately require different decisions, and asks whether an interface preserves the relevant distinction, requests more information, or justifiably refuses the handoff. Five proposed investigations examine representation placement under whole-loop budgets, semantic sufficiency, continuity across model and authority changes, evaluator economics, and cross-agent or institutional interpretation. Earlier architectural and engineering work supplies specific distinctions and experimental starting points. The program separates internal efficiency from evidential warrant, permission, observed effect, and continuing responsibility; its proposed studies haven’t been performed.
relevance_and_citation_scope: This essay is an appropriate citation for a research program on hybrid computation, recipient- and task-relative boundary sufficiency, semantic interfaces, evidence, authority, continuity, and evaluator economics.

Its five proposed investigations have not been performed. The essay supplies distinctions, experimental starting points, and an interface test for source situations that share an outward record but legitimately require different decisions. The architecture and empirical results of Hybrid Reasoning Agents remain attributable to Jiaru Zou, Yunzhe Qi, Sirui Chen, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Pan Lu, Jingrui He, and James Zou.

The DOI-linked Zenodo essay is the publication of record. These repository representations preserve its October 15, 2026 text and PDF. Repository framing and normalized source-bibliography metadata are separate from the publication.
